{

  "answers": [
    {"id":"Q01","answer":"Shuffle all 4 Conflict III cards and place them face down on the bottom; shuffle the 9 II cards and deal 5 face down above them; shuffle the 3 I cards and deal 1 face down on top. Return unused I and II cards unseen to the box.","support":"supported","evidence":"Setup: face-down Conflict Deck construction."},
    {"id":"Q02","answer":"In four-player play a human starts at 1 VP; in three-player play, at 0 VP. Each starts with 2 Agents on the Leader and a third/Swordmaster beside the board; 3 troops in the garrison and 9 in supply; and 1 water.","support":"supported","evidence":"Setup steps 6 and Human component layout."},
    {"id":"Q03","answer":"Yes, you may Reveal while Agents remain, but once you Reveal your turns are skipped for the rest of the phase, so you cannot later take an Agent turn that round. Reveal effects come only from cards revealed for that Reveal turn, not Agent-played cards. At Clean Up, all cards in front of you from Agent and Reveal turns go to your discard pile.","support":"supported","evidence":"Turn Structure: Player Turns and Reveal Turn."},
    {"id":"Q04","answer":"A Plot Intrigue may be played before placing the Agent and resources it grants before entry can pay the cost; effects from the played Agent card or destination occur too late to pay that same cost. One card sends one Agent using one chosen icon. A card with no Agent icons cannot be used for an Agent turn; it may only be revealed.","support":"supported","evidence":"Turn Structure: Plot Intrigue timing and Agent Turn."},
    {"id":"Q05","answer":"At a Combat space, deploy all 3 troops recruited that turn plus up to 2 of the 4 already in your garrison, for up to 5. At a non-Combat space normal deployment is not permitted. Recruited troops come from your supply and are placed in your garrison before deployment.","support":"supported","evidence":"Actions: Recruiting & Deploying Units; Board Space Guide Combat? column."},
    {"id":"Q06","answer":"A Spy Agent icon permits an Agent at a space connected to an observation post where your Spy currently is, without recalling it; the card still needs that icon for this access. Infiltrate recalls your Spy at a connected post to bypass another player's Agent, not your own. Gather Intelligence may recall a connected Spy to draw one card; choose immediately after placement and before space/card effects, and it allows at most one draw per placement. The same Spy cannot pay both Infiltrate and Gather Intelligence, though two different Spies can serve the two effects.","support":"supported","evidence":"Special Rules: Infiltrate, Gather Intelligence, Separate Spy costs and Spy Agent access."},
    {"id":"Q07","answer":"Strength is 2 troops×2 + 1 sandworm×3 + 4 swords = 11. If your last Conflict unit is removed, strength becomes 0. With no unit in the Conflict you cannot participate in Combat Intrigue.","support":"supported","evidence":"Actions: Strength; Phase 3 Combat Intrigue."},
    {"id":"Q08","answer":"Yes. Passing does not prevent you acting later in the window; it closes after all players involved in Combat pass consecutively. After rewards, troops return to their supply, sandworms to the bank, and Combat markers reset to 0.","support":"supported","evidence":"Phase 3: Combat; Resolve Combat cleanup."},
    {"id":"Q09","answer":"In four players, two tied for first each take the second reward; the remaining players compete for the third reward, and nobody takes the Conflict card because there is no winner. In three players, the two tied for first each take second reward, no other reward is given, and nobody takes the card. A player with 0 strength receives no reward.","support":"supported","evidence":"Special Rules: Combat ties; Resolve Combat."},
    {"id":"Q10","answer":"One or more sandworms double rewards once; two do not quadruple them. Control of a location and battle icons on a won Conflict card cannot be doubled. For an optional cost reward, pay the cost a second time to receive it a second time: a 3-spice-for-1-VP offer can be taken twice by paying 6 spice for 2 VP.","support":"supported","evidence":"Sandworm Reward Doubling."},
    {"id":"Q11","answer":"After winning and taking a Conflict card face up into your supply, check it against another face-up Conflict or Objective card there. A matching pair must be flipped face down for 1 VP. At Endgame the wild icon can match any one of the three battle icons in your supply; flip the pair for 1 VP.","support":"supported","evidence":"Battle Icons."},
    {"id":"Q12","answer":"At 2 Influence, gain 1 VP, lose it below 2, and regain it on reaching 2 again. At 4, gain the printed track bonus, which is kept if you fall below 4 and earned again on returning; the first to 4 also takes the Alliance and its 1 VP, which remains only while holding it. Tying the holder does not steal the Alliance; a challenger must rise above them. The separate FAQ trigger for a holder losing Influence after a tie is described in Q38.","support":"supported","evidence":"Scoring: Faction Influence."},
    {"id":"Q13","answer":"During Reveal, Persuasion can be spent before, between, or after Reveal effects. Pool sources to buy one card or split a source across cards; unused Persuasion is lost. The Imperium Row refills to five, and you may buy a replacement immediately if you can afford it. Acquired cards go face up to your discard pile.","support":"supported","evidence":"Acquiring Cards."},
    {"id":"Q14","answer":"At Makers, each unoccupied Maker space gains 1 bonus spice; visiting a Maker space collects all bonus spice there. Deep Desert costs 3 water and offers 4 base spice or, with Hooks, 2 worms; Hagga costs 1 water and offers 2 base spice or, with Hooks, 1 worm. Worms go directly into your own Conflict quadrant, never a garrison. Hooks are required only when the effect specifies them and are retained, not spent. The Shield Wall blocks worm summoning at Arrakeen, Spice Refinery, and Imperial Basin until removed.","support":"supported","evidence":"Phase 4: Makers; Actions: Sandworms; Board Space Guide."},
    {"id":"Q15","answer":"Endgame triggers at the end of a round if anyone has 10+ VP or the Conflict Deck is empty. Players first may play and resolve Endgame Intrigues, then compare VP. Rulebook tiebreakers are spice, then Solari, then water, then garrisoned troops.","support":"supported","evidence":"Scoring / Victory Conditions."},
    {"id":"Q16","answer":"Shuffle the 20 standard contracts and expose 2 face up; the remaining 18 are face down in the bank. Shuffle 4 additional Intrigue cards into that deck and 4 additional Imperium cards into that deck. Shaddam is optional. The 10 contrasting-back contracts are Rise of Ix compatibility cards and stay in the box for standard CHOAM.","support":"supported","evidence":"CHOAM Module: Setup changes; Components."},
    {"id":"Q17","answer":"With CHOAM, a contract icon takes an available face-up public contract and refills the offer from the bank if possible; without CHOAM it gives 2 Solari. If no public contracts remain, gain 2 Solari. A Harvest contract completes by visiting a Maker space and gaining the stated spice total during that turn; Immediate completes when taken; Acquire The Spice Must Flow completes when you next acquire that card.","support":"supported","evidence":"CHOAM Module: Taking contracts; Completing contracts; Human contract icon."},
    {"id":"Q18","answer":"No. You must have held a space contract when you sent the Agent, so one acquired after already visiting that space waits until a future turn. On completion, announce it, gain its rewards, flip it face down, and leave it in your supply.","support":"supported","evidence":"CHOAM Module: Completing contracts; FAQ: Contract completion is mandatory."},
    {"id":"Q19","answer":"Use one shared scoring Rival. It receives the Ornithopter Objective; the two humans receive random other eligible Objectives. First Player is the human whose Objective bears the marker, and the marker alternates between humans. Turn order is First Player → Rival → other human. The Rival never Reveals.","support":"supported","evidence":"Required Rival Rules: Setup; Agent turns."},
    {"id":"Q20","answer":"For an occupied indicated destination, ignore it and reveal another Hagal card. A Place Spy card does not place an Agent: try an empty post of its specified type, otherwise ignore placement, then reveal another card. Ignore ordinary board-space costs and effects and apply only Hagal effects. If the Hagal deck empties or Reshuffle appears, immediately reshuffle it and continue.","support":"supported","evidence":"Required Rival Rules: Agent turns; Place Spy cards."},
    {"id":"Q21","answer":"For 3–4 players, omit Objectives marked for other player counts, shuffle the eligible cards, and give each player one face up; the one showing the First Player marker determines First Player. Shaddam may be chosen only when using CHOAM.","support":"supported","evidence":"Setup steps 3 and 5."},
    {"id":"Q22","answer":"Solari, spice, water, and sandworms are not limited; make a convenient substitution if the bank runs out. If your troop supply is empty, you cannot recruit more until troops return there. Payments of Solari, spice, or water return to the bank.","support":"supported","evidence":"Setup step 7; Recruiting & Deploying Units."},
    {"id":"Q23","answer":"The phases are Round Start, Player Turns, Combat, Makers, Recall. At Round Start reveal a Conflict from the top and place it face up next to the deck, on top of any unclaimed prior Conflict cards; then each player draws five cards. At Recall, if Endgame is not triggered, humans return Agents to Leaders; with 3–4 humans First Player passes clockwise, while in 2P Rival Agents return to supply and First Player passes to the other human.","support":"supported","evidence":"Turn Structure: five phases; Phase 1; Phase 5."},
    {"id":"Q24","answer":"Yes, board-space, Agent-box, and Faction Influence effects may be carried out in any order. Entry costs and requirements must be met before resolving any space or played-card effects, so the visit's Influence cannot satisfy that same visit's entry requirement.","support":"supported","evidence":"Turn Structure: Agent Turn."},
    {"id":"Q25","answer":"An optional arrow cost/effect can be used only once per turn; sandworm doubling of a Conflict reward is the exception. Most card and space effects are mandatory, while “may,” optional arrow costs, and the black-X trash icon are exceptions; direct self-trash instructions are mandatory. Intrigue costs and conditions must be met to play the Intrigue.","support":"supported","evidence":"Special Rules: Arrows / paying costs; FAQ: Mandatory effects and costs."},
    {"id":"Q26","answer":"Place a Spy from your supply on an unoccupied observation post. If you have none in supply, you may first recall one of yours for no effect. If the effect specifies an Agent-icon type connected to the post, that connection is required; otherwise the Spy cannot be placed.","support":"supported","evidence":"Special Rules: Spies & observation posts."},
    {"id":"Q27","answer":"No, Infiltrate cannot bypass your own Agent. A Spy does not provide a free Agent turn: you must play a card with matching normal Agent access or Spy Agent access and pay entry costs. You cannot recall two Spies to get two Gather Intelligence draws on one placement; at most one draw is allowed.","support":"supported","evidence":"Special Rules: Infiltrate and Gather Intelligence; FAQ: Spies."},
    {"id":"Q28","answer":"The controller gets the location bonus whenever any player, including themself, visits: 1 Solari at Arrakeen or Spice Refinery, 1 spice at Imperial Basin. A critical Conflict winner places their Control marker, replacing any opponent's marker. When that Conflict is revealed, the controller may deploy one troop from supply directly to the Conflict, without an Agent visit.","support":"supported","evidence":"Special Rules: Critical Locations & Control."},
    {"id":"Q29","answer":"For a second-place tie, each tied player receives the third reward; the first-place winner keeps the first reward and card, and no further rewards are given. A third-place tie gets nothing. Three tied for first each receive second reward; nobody else receives a reward and no one takes the Conflict card.","support":"supported","evidence":"Special Rules: Combat ties and Three tied for first."},
    {"id":"Q30","answer":"In a three-player game, the top two positive strengths receive first and second rewards; the third place receives nothing. The same applies in a two-human game with its Rival as the third competitor: the Rival is a normal scoring participant, and third reward is used only in a tie for second.","support":"supported","evidence":"Resolve Combat: player-count rewards; Required Rival Rules."},
    {"id":"Q31","answer":"Plot Intrigues may be played on your own Agent or Reveal turns; Combat Intrigues during Combat only if you have a unit in the Conflict; Endgame Intrigues at game end. Keep Intrigues face down, separate from your deck, and reveal only when played; resolved cards go face up in a discard pile beside the Intrigue Deck. If the deck runs out, shuffle its discard into a new deck.","support":"supported","evidence":"Special Rules: Intrigue cards; FAQ: Draw timing."},
    {"id":"Q32","answer":"An ordinary discard instruction discards a card of your choice from hand and cannot discard an Intrigue unless specified. The separate trash-an-Intrigue icon trashes one Intrigue of your choice from hand. Secrets gives one Intrigue selected at random by each opponent who has four or more Intrigues.","support":"supported","evidence":"Special Rules: Discarding; Intrigue cards."},
    {"id":"Q33","answer":"Trash effects may remove cards from hand, discard pile, or in play. Ordinary trashed cards go to the box; Reserve cards return to their Reserve stack. Trashing is optional unless paying a cost or told to trash itself. The Spice Must Flow's acquire VP remains even if the card is later trashed.","support":"supported","evidence":"Trashing; FAQ: Victory."},
    {"id":"Q34","answer":"An acquire-box effect resolves once when acquiring the card. If you cannot draw because your deck is empty, shuffle your discard pile into a new deck and continue. Persuasion cannot be saved; unused Persuasion is lost at the end of Reveal.","support":"supported","evidence":"Acquiring Cards; Special Rules: Acquire box."},
    {"id":"Q35","answer":"Cards played on Agent turns and revealed on your Reveal turn are in play until Clean Up, unless trashed first. Fremen Bond can use one or more other Fremen cards in play; two Bond cards can activate one another regardless of play order. They cease being in play at Clean Up.","support":"supported","evidence":"Special Rules: In play / Fremen Bond."},
    {"id":"Q36","answer":"Recall Agent returns one of your other Agents on the board, not the one just placed; it can act again on a later Agent turn that round. A retreated troop goes from Conflict to your garrison. “Retreat any number” permits zero.","support":"supported","evidence":"Special Rules: Recall Agent icon; Retreat; FAQ: Combat and troops."},
    {"id":"Q37","answer":"A free-choice effect granting two Influence must apply both to one chosen Faction, not split across factions. An Alliance icon requires holding that Faction's Alliance token; an effect with a minimum-Influence requirement requires meeting the stated threshold.","support":"supported","evidence":"Special Rules: Influence."},
    {"id":"Q38","answer":"If the holder loses Influence after being tied, the formerly tied opponent takes the Alliance; if several were tied, the former holder chooses the recipient. If the holder falls to 3 or lower and nobody has 4+, return the Alliance token to the board and the former holder loses its VP.","support":"supported","evidence":"Scoring: Faction Influence; FAQ: Alliance loss."},
    {"id":"Q39","answer":"A card drawn during Reveal is immediately revealed and used that turn. A card drawn after Reveal is kept for next round, in addition to the five cards drawn then. A Plot Intrigue with a later Reveal effect stays face up until Reveal, is used then, and is discarded afterward.","support":"supported","evidence":"FAQ: Draw timing."},
    {"id":"Q40","answer":"No, “when you win” Intrigues cannot be played after tying for first because nobody wins. If received as a reward for an outright win, it may be played immediately.","support":"supported","evidence":"FAQ: Combat and troops."},
    {"id":"Q41","answer":"If VP and all four listed resource tiebreakers remain tied, the player who most recently took a Reveal turn wins. Scores may exceed the printed track's 12.","support":"supported","evidence":"FAQ: Victory."},
    {"id":"Q42","answer":"No. Fulfill all held contracts for a space with the same Agent placement; you cannot delay them after visiting. A contract is another effect of that Agent turn and can resolve in any order with space and Agent-box effects, but it must have been held when sending the Agent.","support":"supported","evidence":"FAQ: Contract completion is mandatory."},
    {"id":"Q43","answer":"Shaddam does not start with the two reserved Sardaukar contracts; they are set aside before the initial shuffle. Only he may acquire them, choosing one instead of a generally available contract. His Signet Ring deployment restriction takes effect immediately when played to send an Agent and lasts for that turn only, not the full round.","support":"supported","evidence":"CHOAM Module: Setup changes; Reserved Sardaukar contracts; FAQ: Shaddam."},
    {"id":"Q44","answer":"Feyd's token starts on the leftmost Training track space and remains on the rightmost space after reaching it. Lady Jessica begins with her Lady Jessica side face up. Reverend Mother Jessica may use her ability on the turn she flips.","support":"supported","evidence":"Special Rules: Leader clarifications; FAQ."},
    {"id":"Q45","answer":"Moving from 1 to 3 counts as reaching 2, and it can count again later if you lose Influence and later move up through 2 again. Moving downward through 2 does not count. Clean Up moving Spacing Guild's Favor from play to discard does not trigger its discard ability; only discarding it from hand does.","support":"supported","evidence":"Special Rules: Leader clarifications."},
    {"id":"Q46","answer":"Accept Contract is Spice Trade access, no cost, no Combat; always draw a card and resolve the contract icon (without CHOAM gain 2 Solari; with CHOAM take/refill a public contract, or get 2 Solari if offers are exhausted). It gives no automatic Influence. Dutiful Service is Emperor access, no cost, no Combat; gain 1 Emperor Influence and resolve the same contract icon. It automatically advances Emperor once, not twice; it is a Faction space.","support":"supported","evidence":"Board Space Guide; Faction status of the contract spaces; shared human contract icon rule."},
    {"id":"Q47","answer":"Arrakeen: City access, no cost, Combat yes; controller gets 1 Solari, visitor recruits one troop and draws one card. Fremkit: Fremen access, no cost, Combat yes; gain 1 Fremen Influence and draw a card. Research Station: City access, costs 2 water, Combat yes; recruit two troops and draw two cards.","support":"supported","evidence":"Board Space Guide — Standard 2–4 Players."},
    {"id":"Q48","answer":"Deep Desert: Spice Trade, 3 water, 4 base spice or (with Hooks) 2 sandworms. Hagga Basin: Spice Trade, 1 water, 2 base spice or (with Hooks) 1 sandworm. Collect all bonus spice at either space even when choosing worms. Hooks are not spent.","support":"supported","evidence":"Board Space Guide; Actions: Sandworms."},
    {"id":"Q49","answer":"Both options require City access and 2+ Fremen Influence, with no resource entry cost. Option one: take Hooks if lacking them, recruit one troop, gain 1 water. Option two: gain 1 water and optionally remove the Shield Wall; it gives no troop.","support":"supported","evidence":"Board Space Guide: Sietch Tabr."},
    {"id":"Q50","answer":"High Council is Landsraad access, costs 5 Solari on each visit, and is not a Combat space. First visit places your Councilor on an unoccupied seat and gives 2 Persuasion on every Reveal turn for the rest of the game. Subsequent visits give 2 spice, draw an Intrigue, and recruit three troops.","support":"supported","evidence":"Board Space Guide: High Council."},
    {"id":"Q51","answer":"Swordmaster is Landsraad access, not Combat. It costs 8 Solari before anyone gains a Swordmaster and 6 afterward; once per player per game. Take the third Agent onto your Leader, available this round and for the rest of the game. A Rival gaining one also lowers human cost to 6.","support":"supported","evidence":"Board Space Guide: Swordmaster."},
    {"id":"Q52","answer":"Imperial Privilege is Landsraad access, not Combat; costs 3 Solari and requires 2+ Emperor Influence. You may discard an Intrigue to draw one; recall one of your other Agents and draw a card. It does not automatically give Emperor Influence.","support":"supported","evidence":"Board Space Guide: Imperial Privilege."},
    {"id":"Q53","answer":"Shipping is Spice Trade access, not Combat; costs 3 spice and requires 2+ Spacing Guild Influence. Gain 5 Solari and 1 Influence with any one Faction; it need not be Guild.","support":"supported","evidence":"Board Space Guide: Shipping."},
    {"id":"Q54","answer":"Gather Support is Landsraad, not Combat: choose 0 or 2 Solari to recruit two troops; paying 2 also gives 1 water. Spice Refinery is City, Combat: choose 0 or 1 spice to gain 2 or 4 Solari respectively; its controller separately gains 1 Solari.","support":"supported","evidence":"Board Space Guide: Gather Support; Spice Refinery."},
    {"id":"Q55","answer":"Heighliner: Guild access, costs 5 spice, gain 1 Guild Influence and recruit 5; Combat yes. Desert Tactics: Fremen, costs 1 water, gain 1 Fremen Influence, recruit 1, optionally trash a card; Combat yes. Sardaukar: Emperor, costs 4 spice, gain 1 Emperor Influence, draw an Intrigue, recruit 4; Combat no.","support":"supported","evidence":"Board Space Guide entries for Heighliner, Desert Tactics, Sardaukar."},
    {"id":"Q56","answer":"Assembly Hall: Landsraad, no cost, not Combat; draw an Intrigue and gain 1 Persuasion during your Reveal turn if your Agent is there. Espionage: Bene Gesserit, costs 1 spice, not Combat; gain 1 Bene Gesserit Influence, draw a card, place a Spy. Deliver Supplies: Spacing Guild, no cost, not Combat; gain 1 Guild Influence and 1 water.","support":"supported","evidence":"Board Space Guide entries for Assembly Hall, Espionage, Deliver Supplies."},
    {"id":"Q57","answer":"False Orders makes affected opponents move their Spy to an empty post not connected to your Agent's destination that turn. It may be played even if no enemy Spy is connected there. Litany Against Fear's red box is ignored during Reveal, or when it gains an Agent icon and is played normally as an Agent card.","support":"supported","evidence":"FAQ: Leader/card rulings."},
    {"id":"Q58","answer":"Opponents cannot acquire the card removed by Manipulate. You may acquire it by other means but without the 1-Persuasion discount. If it has not been acquired by the end of your next Reveal, remove it from the game.","support":"supported","evidence":"FAQ: Manipulate."},
    {"id":"Q60","answer":"The Rival starts with four Influence cubes, 3 troops in garrison and 9 in supply, 2 Agents in supply and the third beside the board, 3 Spies, 1 water, and score and Combat markers at 0. Shuffle House Hagal and retain the 2P Reshuffle card. The Rival is a scoring competitor; its 10+ VP triggers Endgame at Recall and it can win.","support":"supported","evidence":"Required Rival Rules: Setup; Rival starting components."},
    {"id":"Q61","answer":"As soon as its Solari, spice, Intrigue cards and water total reaches its printed Swordmaster value, it spends exactly that many and takes its third Agent, usable that round. Count each unit/resource/card as one. Mandatory spending order is Solari, spice, Intrigue, water; use each type fully as needed before the next, stopping at cost and keeping leftovers. The Agent is immediately usable.","support":"supported","evidence":"Required Rival Rules: Swordmaster resource total and spending priority."},
    {"id":"Q62","answer":"After Swordmaster, spend each set of 7 Solari, 7 spice, 3 Intrigue cards, or 3 water for 1 VP. A mixed total of seven does not qualify; only the exact listed sets do.","support":"supported","evidence":"Required Rival Rules: After Swordmaster."},
    {"id":"Q63","answer":"The Rival chooses the Faction with least Influence, breaking ties by the leftmost priority icon. It gains VP for reaching 2 and Alliance VP like a human, but gets no resource bonus for reaching 4 Influence. A numbered Hagal Influence icon refers to that position in its Faction priority list.","support":"supported","evidence":"Required Rival Rules: After Swordmaster; Rival turns; Combat."},
    {"id":"Q64","answer":"No. Choose only the destination matching the current condition—Guild Influence for Accept Contract/Shipping, Conflict tier for Deliver Supplies/Heighliner. If that selected destination is occupied, reveal another Hagal card rather than using the other destination.","support":"supported","evidence":"Required Rival Rules: Agent turns."},
    {"id":"Q65","answer":"Yes. At every Combat space the Rival deploys up to two available garrison troops even if that card recruits none. At a noncombat space newly recruited troops go to its garrison. An unmet conditional 2+ Influence bonus is simply omitted and does not prevent Agent placement.","support":"supported","evidence":"Required Rival Rules: Agent turns."},
    {"id":"Q66","answer":"For an unrestricted placement, use the first available Faction observation post in priority order; if all four are occupied, ignore placement. Placing the third and final supply Spy immediately recalls its other two Spies and triggers its Scheme. The Rival never recalls Spies to Infiltrate or Gather Intelligence.","support":"supported","evidence":"Required Rival Rules: Spies and Schemes."},
    {"id":"Q67","answer":"Troops recruited by a Scheme before Agent placement can deploy if the Rival visits a Combat space that same turn. If a Place Spy card finds no legal post, ignore placement and reveal another Hagal card because it has not sent an Agent.","support":"supported","evidence":"Required Rival Rules: Spies and Schemes; Place Spy cards."},
    {"id":"Q68","answer":"The Rival takes all accumulated bonus spice at the Maker space. At Hagga or Deep Desert, if it has Hooks and the Conflict allows worms, it summons one or two respectively instead of taking base spice; if it summons none, it gets base spice (2 or 4). Without Hooks it takes base spice. A protected Conflict prevents summoning while the Wall remains, so it takes base spice; Imperial Basin always gives 1 base spice. Hooks are retained.","support":"supported","evidence":"Required Rival Rules: Maker spaces; Actions: Sandworms."},
    {"id":"Q69","answer":"At the beginning of Combat, if the Rival has at least one deployed unit, reveal one Hagal card and add its bottom swords to strength; on Reshuffle, reshuffle and reveal again. Humans then have their normal Combat Intrigue window. A Rival with no unit gets no such bonus.","support":"supported","evidence":"Required Rival Rules: Combat."},
    {"id":"Q70","answer":"Yes: it gains control bonuses on visits and defensive troops when its controlled Conflict is revealed, wins cards and battle-icon VP normally, and doubles rewards if it has a sandworm. It always takes optional Conflict VP if it can pay/recall required Spies. It never takes contracts; a contract reward gives it 2 Solari, even with CHOAM.","support":"supported","evidence":"Required Rival Rules: Combat."},
    {"id":"Q71","answer":"During Reveal effects, total and announce strength and set the Combat marker at any point; you may update it as strength changes during Reveal. If Combat Intrigue alters units or strength, adjust the marker when that card resolves in the Combat Intrigue window. Strength above 20 uses the +20 side and starts again from the beginning of the track.","support":"supported","evidence":"Reveal Turn; Strength; Phase 3: Combat."},
    {"id":"Q72","answer":"A Leader's Signet Ring ability activates when you play Signet Ring on one of your Agent turns, not merely when you reveal that card. Cards of any type can override the usual rules of the game.","support":"supported","evidence":"Setup step 3; Overview."},
    {"id":"Q73","answer":"A Recall Spy icon returns one of your Spies from an observation post to your supply, usually as a cost for an effect. It is a separate icon and is not automatically Infiltrate or Gather Intelligence; those abilities have their own conditions and timing.","support":"supported","evidence":"Special Rules: Spies & observation posts; Separate Spy costs."},
    {"id":"Q74","answer":"The trash-an-Intrigue icon trashes one Intrigue of your choice from your hand. An ordinary discard instruction chooses from your hand but cannot discard an Intrigue unless it says so.","support":"supported","evidence":"Trashing; Discarding."},
    {"id":"Q75","answer":"A sandworm-doubled reward that grants one Influence can be paid a second time, giving a second Influence; the two may go to the same or two different Factions.     {"id":"Q76","answer":"Resolve the Signet Ring ability printed on the selected Rival card, not its Scheme.     {"id":"Q81","answer":"Each human begins with one Influence cube at the bottom of each of the four Faction tracks.     {"id":"Q82","answer":"First Player takes the first turn, then play proceeds clockwise, one Agent or Reveal turn at a time.     {"id":"Q83","answer":"The steps are Reveal Cards, Resolve Reveal Effects, then Clean Up.
